thread.title: What Are Some Of The Tradable Impacts Of Apple Moving To All OLED Screens This Fall?

author: Trent Welsh
title: What Are Some Of The Tradable Impacts Of Apple Moving To All OLED Screens This Fall?
text:
Rumors are starting to circulate that Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) plans on moving to OLED screens for all of its upcoming iPhone models this fall, which might be a short-term windfall for battered Universal Display Corporation ( OLED ). Universal Display holds many of the patents that underlie OLED technology, which looks to maybe dominate the iPhone market for the next two to three years at least, if Apple does switch to all OLED screens starting this fall. This also sounds terrific for Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. ( OTC:SSNLF ), which is currently the only OLED screen provider for the iPhone X model. However, Apple is continually trying to diversify its suppliers, which means that maybe the OLED ramp up by LG Display Company Ltd. ( LPL ) over the first half of the year has gone well enough that it can now take over as another partial supplier for Apple's OLED iPhone screens this coming fall.
According to a report by South Korea's Electronic Times, Apple hopes to use OLED for all of its upcoming iPhone screens instead of using LCD screens for its lower end models like the current iPhone 8 and the iPhone 8 Plus. This might be a short-term boon for Universal Display whose stock has been hammered over 2018 because investors are always looking ahead for the next best thing in technology.
OLED data by YCharts
If Apple does move to all OLED screens this fall, Universal Display might be a nice buy at this time, at a sub-$100 per share price tag, as it is now trading at approximately half the value it did in early 2018. Apple's move to all OLED screens means that it might have 3-5 years of dominance left in this technology before new technologies potentially start to take its market share. Universal display moved 12.4% on the initial Apple report meaning that I could easily see the stock moving into the $110-$120 range again pretty quickly if Apple can get away from LCD screens. The stock could really take off if the upcoming Apple refresh cycle is markedly better than last years, which featured the ultra expensive ~ $1000 iPhone X, with one of the upcoming headlines being the superior OLED screens now on every new iPhone produced.
One of the reason's that Apple might be able to move to an all OLED iPhone lineup this fall is the possible success LG Display might be having in its attempt to become an Apple OLED iPhone screen supplier. LG Display is already a major player in the OLED space by being a significant supplier of OLED based television screens. Making superior small OLED screens for iPhones though is a tough proposition though, and is one reason why Samsung has a monopoly in the space currently for the iPhone X. It is not a given that because LG Display can make great OLED television screens, that it can easily make iPhone screens that meet Apple's stringent demands. An example of failure in initiatives like this can be seen with the former sapphire glass debacle , which involved billions in investments by Apple into the company GT Advanced Technologies, which ultimately failed to meet Apple's needs.
Apple has again put its money where its mouth is though by investing billions in OLED technology by helping LG Display make the transition towards possibly being an iPhone OLED screen supplier. The one main rule of being in the Apple supplier club unfortunately though is that you do not talk about being in the Apple supplier club. This means that news surrounding upcoming iPhone models are as secret as Apple can possibly make them by keeping a close eye not only on its own employees, but also all of its parts suppliers. Fortunately, a lot of times, where there is smoke, there is fire, and here is the list of events leading up to LG Display potentially making a huge splash in the upcoming iPhone cycle later this fall as an OLED screen supplier.
May 29, 2018 LG Display +4.1% on iPhone OLED panel report
Dec. 26, 2017 South Korea approves LG Display's $4.4B OLED plant
Dec. 7, 2017 LG Display could supply OLED panels for iPhone X
Oct. 11, 2017 Apple plans flexible OLEDs with LG, not Samsung
July 28, 2017 Apple paying LG Display $2.67B for OLED panels
July 26, 2017 Was Apple behind LG Display's $7B OLED push?
LG Display has had the time by now to get its plants and lines in order for significant OLED panel production both for televisions as well as iPhone screens. It also has had enough time to produce and test potential screens with Apple to start production this summer for this fall's lineup of iPhones as long as there weren't too many setbacks. However, many details won't be known to investors, due to Apple's secrecy, until techies can start breaking down the new iPhones into parts, and until LG Display starts talking about OLED profit numbers, or other hints in its quarterly reports, including references to any significant new unnamed customers.
This uncertainty, along with the fact that LG Display's legacy LCD business is anything but exciting to investors with its shrinking margins, means that the company trades at a tremendous value with a trailing P/E ratio of 7.79. It currently sports a market cap of only $7.6 billion dollars while its revenues in 2017 exceeded $25 billion dollars. If LG Display can successfully produce OLED screens for Apple's upcoming iPhones, by meeting Apple's lofty expectations, there is tons of upside to this company I believe as GBH Insights predicts that this year's Apple iPhone release could sell up to 350 million units over the next 12-18 months. GBH predicts a more modestly priced iPhone X model in the $700-$800 range, with a brand new iPhone X Plus premium model for those wanting something closer to the $1000 mark. If Apple can market a premium all OLED iPhone lineup this fall with better pricing on its models, it's stock could be in line for that final move up to the $200 range, or a mere ~5% up from its latest close. It has the momentum in place, now it just has to build some consumer excitement.
AAPL data by YCharts
If LG Display can start to leave its legacy business behind and make the transition to the much higher margin OLED, I would expect that company's trailing P/E ratio could easily trade up into the 15 range which means that LP Display is a potential double from its current levels to about $20 a share if things go well. I don't believe this is a stretch as all the other companies in this article have much healthier trailing P/E multiples such as 47.63 for Universal Display, 369.32 for Samsung, and even a 18.36 trailing P/E ratio for Apple according to Seeking Alpha. LG Display is risky, but limited I believe because of its already low valuation, while the potential rewards could be pretty lucrative if the company was able to develop the screens Apple so desperately wants for its upcoming iPhone cycle.
One of the biggest risks for all of these companies moving forward is can they stay on the cutting edge of technology and grow and change over time. Or, will they be become an aging dinosaur with legacy products that companies like LG Display are currently known for? One of the many possible future screen technology moves include a move to MicroLED screens, that Apple is currently working on, although results aren't likely for another 3-5 years at the least. Apple is a great bet as a long-term winner based on its market dominance, but I plan on trading in and out of Universal Display and LG Display when I hit nice profit levels, or if the story changes and moves suddenly in a new direction. I continue to be long Apple and LG Display, and am considering a purchase here soon of Universal Display if it continues to trade under $100 a share. Best of luck to all.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL, LPL.
